facts.fact: A UNICEF and UN Legal Identity Agenda case study states that the Department of Civil Registration of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security manages the system, which stores births, adoptions, marriages, divorces and deaths in the NPRS, with the Prime Minister's Office leading and coordinating; no date is given, so the published date is used.
The case study states that the digital facilities were developed within the country with its own resources; it gives no budget figure and no date, so the published date is used.

The case study states that a CRVS Strategic Plan was formulated in 2014-15 and approved by Cabinet, and that the national CRVS Technical Committee set up to implement it, chaired by the Ministry of Home Affairs, remains in place; it names no later plan.
The case study's milestones give the NPRS as established in 2011, its death registration module deployed in 2012 and its birth registration module in 2013, with the marriage module following in 2014.

The case study states that births and deaths are registered electronically in real time in the NPRS at local registration centres, while marriages are entered in it at head office only and customary marriages and divorces are not recorded; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The case study states that all local registration centres are connected to the NPRS, enabling real-time electronic registration of births and deaths into it, and that birth and death certificates are issued locally and on the spot from the NPRS; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The case study states that birth and death registration takes place in 62 local registration centres (it lists 14 regional offices, 24 Category I and 21 Category II sub-regional offices, which sum to 59), with 24 health facilities and hospitals also registering, and that all the local registration centres are connected to the NPRS; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The same case study lists among its challenges that the lack of connectivity to the NPRS in certain sub-regional offices continues to hinder timely capture of records and verification for duplicate documents, with no count of those offices; no date is given, so the published date is used.
